name: doctor
title: Check toolchain
description: Report tool versions, paths, SDK and KVM readiness, and next_steps: what is left to set up, in order. Without a virtual iOS device profile, its step names the next stage of the setup chain (next_stage) and carries the whole chain in order (stage, what, done true, false or null when only the person's files or a later check can tell, how, ask_first). With a profile, steps name only what stops the next start: a profile ios.virtual.status refuses, too little disk space, a failed last start, or apps the last start did not install.

name: capabilities
title: What this computer can do
description: Summarise in one call what this computer can do right now, to plan before building or starting anything: Android builds, the Android emulator (with its AVDs), connected Android devices, iOS builds with xtool, connected iPhones and the virtual iPhone (configured, running, phase). Each has ready and missing, the names of what it lacks; doctor's next_steps say how to set them up. Runs doctor's tool checks, so it takes a few seconds.

name: desktop.status
title: Desktop status
description: Read recent jobs and live preview sessions for the desktop panel.

name: desktop.open
title: Open Tomacco
description: Show an existing desktop session or start one, opening the requested workspace tab.

session.description: Running preview session name; defaults to main

file.description: Project-relative source file to reveal in the files tab

device_only.description: Start the desktop without showing its main window, for a detached device window. A desktop that is already running is left as it is.

name: settings.get
title: Settings
description: Read configured tool locations and update settings.

name: settings.configure
title: Set up toolchain
description: Configure SDK, JDK and executable paths without installing or running them, how updates behave, and how many heavy jobs run at once.

executables.description: Tool name to absolute executable path

mode.description: off: no request unless the user asks. notify: check once a day and tell the user. auto: also install when idle.

token_file.description: Owner-only file with a GitHub token, for a private repository; empty removes it

jobs.description: How many heavy jobs run at once; more wait as queued with a reason. 0 means no limit

max_builds.description: Builds and deploys (project.execute, project.run except Flutter sessions, ios.flutter_build); 2 by default

max_emulators.description: Android emulators started with android.avd_start, for as long as they run; no limit by default

name: catalog.list
title: Device catalog
description: List built-in and custom device profiles with provenance.

name: catalog.import
title: Import models
description: Validate and atomically import custom device profile JSON. Built-ins are immutable.

name: catalog.export
title: Export model
description: Export a profile to a new JSON file.

name: catalog.remove
title: Remove custom model
description: Remove a custom profile by ID.

name: project.inspect
title: Open project
description: Detect frameworks and available platforms without executing project code. For a Gradle build, android lists each app module's application ID, namespace, min, target and compile SDK, build types, flavors and variants as read from the build files and versions catalog; values only Gradle can compute are listed under unresolved.

name: project.configure
title: Configure project
description: Save the deployment application ID and explicit command-array tasks; update xtool's bundleID when applicable.

tasks.description: Task names mapped to argv arrays; replaces configured tasks

name: project.create
title: Create project
description: Create a native Android app, a Jetpack Compose app in Kotlin with one UI test (kind compose), an Android app with Swift core, SwiftUI iOS app (xtool), or Flutter app in a new directory. With build:true, an xtool project is also built in the same job; project.app then names the .app.

name: project.plan
title: View build plan
description: Resolve exact commands, working directory and expected artifacts without executing them.

task.description: Name of an explicitly configured project task

name: project.execute
title: Start build / test
description: Execute a build, tests, lint or named project task as a durable cancellable job. An identical active request reuses its job; different work for the occupied project returns workspace_busy with the active job. Use job.send for Flutter Hot Reload.

task.description: Name of an explicitly configured project task

name: project.run
title: Build & run on device
description: Build and deploy to a selected Android/iOS device. Flutter supports interactive hot reload via job.send. An identical active request reuses its job; different work for the occupied project returns workspace_busy with the active job. Use job.send for Flutter Hot Reload.

bundle_id.description: Android application ID for Gradle projects (default: the variant's ID read from the build files, or tomacco.json's applicationId), or exact installed iPhone bundle ID to resolve ambiguous xtool signing mappings. Omit for automatic iPhone detection.

variant.description: Gradle build variant to install, such as freeDebug. Required when the app has product flavors; otherwise the configuration's build type.

name: project.dependency_updates
title: Check dependency updates
description: Compare the versions a Gradle build declares, in gradle/libs.versions.toml and its build files, with the newest versions in Maven metadata from Google Maven, Maven Central and the Gradle Plugin Portal. Read-only, as a job whose report.json lists each dependency and plugin with its source line, latest stable and latest version and a status. Answers offline at once when no repository host resolves.

repositories.description: Maven repository base URLs (https:// or file:///) to ask in order instead of the defaults

name: project.import_xcode
title: Import Xcode project
description: Write an xtool adapter package for an .xcodeproj with the pinned omarchy-apple-dev xcodeproj2xtool.py, by default in omarchy-xtool beside the project. Returns what the generator could not map as warnings. Build the adapter with project.execute. Needs only ios.toolkit_install's checkout.

target.description: Application target, when the project has several

out.description: Absolute path of the adapter directory

name: project.app
title: Find built iOS app
description: Report the built xtool/*.app of an xtool project, its bundle identifier, and whether the virtual device's bundle rules accept it, with the calls that come next. Reads files only.

name: job.list
title: Jobs
description: List durable jobs including status and artifacts, newest first. Filter by state, by the operation that started the job (a prefix such as project. or android.sdk_install; jobs from before this was recorded have none), by project directory and by creation time. For the next page pass the id of the last job as before.

state.description: Only jobs in one of these states

operation.description: Only jobs started by an operation whose name starts with this

project.description: Absolute directory: only jobs that lock it or run in it or below it

since.description: Only jobs created at or after this time, in seconds since 1970

before.description: A job ID: only jobs created before it, for the next page

name: job.get
title: Job status
description: Get plan, status, exit code and SHA-256 artifact metadata.

name: job.logs
title: Live logs
description: Read incremental log bytes; pass next_offset on the next call.

name: job.wait
title: Wait for job
description: Wait up to 60 seconds for a job; running is a valid nonterminal result.

name: job.events
title: Job timeline
description: A job's state changes (queued, running and how it ended, with exit code and error), phase changes (such as waiting, queued, building, ready) with their reason, retries and cancellation requests, each with a time in seconds since 1970, in order. Pass next_after as after to read only newer events. Jobs from before events were recorded get their creation and end from the job record, marked synthesized.

after.description: Return only events with a larger id

name: job.cancel
title: Cancel job
description: Cancel a job and terminate its child process group.

name: job.send
title: Hot Reload
description: Send reload, restart or quit to a running Flutter session.

name: storage.prune
title: Clean up old jobs and reports
description: List, and with apply remove, what Tomacco keeps of finished work under its data directory: records and logs of jobs that ended before older_than_days, log files without a job, and report directories under reports/. A dry run by default; also reports the size of each top-level entry of the data directory. Never touches queued or running jobs, emulators, SDKs, the virtual iOS device, settings, or artifacts in projects.

max_job_log_mb.description: Also remove the oldest finished jobs until their logs take at most this much

apply.description: Remove the candidates; without it nothing is changed

name: diagnostics.bundle
title: Write a bug report bundle
description: Write one .tar.gz for a bug report on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere. It holds the version, a host summary (OS, kernel, CPUs, memory, KVM, desktop session), doctor, the settings, and for the most recent failed, timed-out or cancelled jobs their record, timeline and the end of their log. Recognised secrets are masked, job environments keep only variable names, and the home directory is shown as ~. Masking recognises known shapes only: the person should read the bundle before sharing it. Returns the path, size, SHA-256 and the files it holds.

path.description: Absolute .tar.gz file to write; by default a new file under diagnostics/ in the data directory

jobs.description: How many recent jobs that did not succeed to include

log_kb.description: How much of the end of each job's log to include

name: device.list

name: device.info

description: Read Android properties/display settings or iOS device information.

paths.description: Absolute paths: APKs, one .aab or one .ipa

name: device.screenshot

description: Capture the real device display and wait up to 30 seconds. MCP returns the PNG inline, with artifact metadata.

name: device.logs
title: Device logs
description: Capture bounded logcat/syslog output as a job; optionally filter by app or tag. On Android 12 and newer, bundle_id selects the app by its user ID, also across restarts and before launch; older Android needs the app running.

name: android.input
title: Tap / swipe / input
description: Control real Android UI through adb, using device pixel coordinates. ASCII text is typed; other text is pasted through the device clipboard with the configured scrcpy 4.1 server on Android 7 and newer.

name: android.hierarchy
title: Read UI tree
description: Read Android's UIAutomator XML hierarchy.

name: android.launch

description: Resolve the installed launcher activity and wait for the actual launch result.

name: android.record

description: Record an Android screen video and pull it to the given path.

name: android.mirror
title: Show Android live
description: Open scrcpy with keyboard and pointer control for the selected device.

name: android.deep_link
title: Open deep link
description: Open a deep link on the selected Android device.

name: android.performance
title: Performance report
description: Collect actual memory, frame timing, battery or package reports.

name: android.ports
title: Connect dev server
description: Create/remove adb reverse or forward TCP ports.

name: android.permission
title: App permission
description: Grant or revoke a runtime permission for a selected app.

name: android.settings
title: Device settings for tests
description: Read or set what changes an app's look and motion in UI tests and screenshots: dark mode, font scale, animations, airplane mode and one app's language. Arguments left out stay as they are; the result reads every setting back and reports a value Android did not apply as setting_not_applied.

dark_mode.description: System dark theme; auto follows the device schedule

font_scale.description: System font size; 1 is the default

animations.description: false sets the window, transition and animator scales to 0; true sets them to 1

bundle_id.description: App whose language app_locale sets and the result reads

app_locale.description: Language tags separated by commas, such as de-DE or fr,en; empty follows the device language again. Android 13 and newer.

name: android.display
title: Display orientation and size
description: Lock the screen orientation, override the display size or density, or reset them, on a phone or emulator; the result reads all three back. A value Android did not apply answers setting_not_applied. With no other argument it only reads.

orientation.description: Lock the rotation; auto follows the sensor again

width.description: Override width in pixels, with height

height.description: Override height in pixels, with width

reset.description: Return size and density to the device's own and rotation to the sensor, before anything else given

name: android.notifications
title: Notifications
description: List the notifications Android is showing, with key, package, title, text, channel and flags; open or close the notification shade; or snooze one notification by its key. Every action returns the list afterwards. adb cannot cancel another app's notifications, so snooze hides one for a time instead.

action.description: open and close expand or collapse the notification shade

key.description: Notification key from the list, for snooze

seconds.description: How long snooze hides the notification

name: android.app_files
title: App data files
description: List or pull the private files of a debuggable app (its data directory, through run-as). pull returns a job that writes the files as one .tar archive. Release builds answer app_not_debuggable. To clear app data or force-stop the app, use device.app.

bundle_id.description: Application ID of a debuggable build

path.description: File or directory inside the app's data directory, relative to it, such as files or databases/app.db

output.description: Absolute local path of the .tar archive, for pull

name: android.each
title: Run on every Android device
description: Run the same steps on every connected Android device, or on the listed ones, as one job: all devices at once, each device's steps in order until one fails. A step that returns a job is followed to its end. The job's report.json artifact has every device's result; the job fails if any device failed. Steps leave out device and platform, which are set per device.

arguments.description: The operation's arguments without device and platform

devices.description: Serials from device.list; all online Android devices when left out

name: android.connect
title: Android over Wi-Fi
description: Pair or connect adb to a device address. Pairing codes are not persisted.

retry.description: Try again after a failure: count more attempts (at most 5), waiting backoff_seconds, doubled each time up to 600. Only adb connect is repeated, never pairing; the result says how many attempts it took.

name: android.calibrate
title: Read model from device
description: Create a custom profile from actual wm size/density. Frame details remain editable.

name: android.sdk_packages
title: SDK packages
description: List available/installed Android SDK packages.

name: android.sdk_install
title: Install SDK packages
description: Install explicit SDK package IDs. License acceptance is opt-in.

retry.description: Try again after a failure: count more attempts (at most 5), waiting backoff_seconds, doubled each time up to 600. A cancelled or timed-out job is not repeated; the job's result lists its attempts.

name: android.avds
title: Android emulators
description: List configured Android emulators with model profile, resolution, density, GPU mode and installed system images. Legacy profiles are inferred only from unique resolution/density matches.

name: android.avd_create
title: Create emulator
description: Create an AVD using an installed system image and a catalogue profile.

name: android.avd_profile
title: Set emulator display
description: Apply a profile's resolution/density to a stopped Tomacco AVD.

name: android.avd_configure
title: Set emulator performance
description: Persist graphics, RAM and CPU settings for a stopped registered Android emulator. Preserves app data and other configuration, saves the original configuration, and skips incompatible VM snapshots on subsequent Tomacco starts. Running AVDs are rejected.

vulkan.description: Vulkan compatibility override; off keeps OpenGL ES and avoids the Vulkan interoperability path. Requires a cold restart.

name: android.avd_start
title: Start emulator
description: Start or reuse an Android virtual device. CPU acceleration remains enabled independently of the selected GPU renderer.

gpu.description: configured respects the saved AVD renderer; auto selects a compatible renderer; host uses the computer GPU. An override applies to this start. Changing renderer requires stopping the emulator first.

cold_boot.description: Skip saved VM snapshots, for example after changing the GPU renderer. App data is retained.

audio.description: Enable the emulator host audio backend independently of headless mode. Embedded clients can disable this and use runtime.audio instead. Applied only to a new emulator process.

vulkan.description: Vulkan compatibility override; off keeps OpenGL ES and avoids the Vulkan interoperability path. Requires a cold restart.

name: android.emulator
title: Control emulator
description: Stop an emulator; save, load, list or delete its snapshots; set its GPS location, battery or network speed and latency through the emulator console. A command the console refuses answers emulator_refused.

name.description: Snapshot name for snapshot-save, snapshot-load and snapshot-delete

battery_level.description: Battery charge in percent, for battery

charging.description: Whether the charger is connected, for battery

network_speed.description: Network speed preset, for network; full means no limit

network_delay.description: Network latency, for network: gprs 150-550 ms, edge 80-400 ms, umts 35-200 ms, none adds no latency

name: android.package_inspect
title: Inspect APK or AAB
description: Read an APK or AAB without a device: package, version name and code, minimum, target and compile SDK, permissions, native ABIs and signing certificates with their SHA-256 digests. APKs go through aapt2 and apksigner from the SDK build-tools; an AAB's manifest is read directly and its signature through keytool. Reads the file only.

path.description: Absolute path of an .apk or .aab file

name: ios.sdk_install
title: Import Apple SDK
description: Import the SDK from an Apple Xcode archive you downloaded yourself, with xtool. Tomacco downloads nothing from Apple. Read Xcode's license first.

name: ios.toolkit_install
title: Install iOS toolkit
description: Fetch the pinned commit of Joshua Warren's omarchy-apple-dev into Tomacco's data directory as a job. With toolchain:true, also run its install-toolchain.sh --mode full --user-only under a private HOME there: it builds a private xtool fork and helpers, and imports the Xcode archive you name in xcode_xip into a private SDK separate from ios.sdk_install. Never runs sudo or an AUR helper, never downloads from Apple, and leaves your own xtool, SDK and Swift alone. Read Xcode's license first.

xcode_xip.description: Absolute path of an Xcode.xip or Xcode.app you downloaded from Apple yourself

name: ios.flutter_setup
title: Prepare Flutter for iOS
description: Run the pinned omarchy-apple-dev flutter/setup.sh as a job, once per Flutter version: it downloads about 7 GB from Google's servers, builds gen_snapshot for iOS on Linux, and replaces that one file in your Flutter install, keeping the original beside it. UNTESTED in Tomacco.

name: ios.flutter_build
title: Build Flutter app for iOS
description: Build an unsigned Runner.ipa and Runner.app for arm64 iPhones on Linux with the pinned omarchy-apple-dev flutter/build.sh, as a durable job. Release mode only; plugins must ship a Package.swift. Dart defines appear in the job record, so pass no secrets. UNTESTED in Tomacco.

target.description: Dart entry point, relative to the project

name: ios.crash_symbolicate
title: Read crash report
description: Read a modern JSON .ips crash report with the pinned omarchy-apple-dev ips-symbolicate.py. Returns the exception, the faulting thread and its frames. Frames resolve against the Mach-O files in binaries, matched by LC_UUID. Needs only ios.toolkit_install's checkout.

binaries.description: Absolute paths of local Mach-O files, such as the app's executable

name: ios.ipa_inspect
title: Inspect iOS app
description: Read what an .ipa archive or .app directory says about itself, without a device or an Apple tool: bundle_id, version, build, minimum_os, device_family, architectures, the executable's code signature (signed, ad_hoc, identifier, team_id and the signing certificate's common_name, organizational_unit, not_after and sha1), its embedded entitlements, and provisioning_profile, a summary of embedded.mobileprovision (name, uuid, team_id, team_name, expires, expired, days_left, kind development/ad-hoc/app-store/enterprise, devices count, certificates, bundle_id_matches, signing_certificate_included) or null. warnings names an expired profile, a profile for another bundle or team, a signer the profile does not list, a missing arm64 slice and an unsigned executable. Nothing is verified cryptographically: the files are read as they claim to be. Reads files only.

path.description: Absolute local path of an .ipa archive or an .app directory

name: ios.store_ship
title: Prepare for App Store
description: Build an App Store IPA from an xtool project with the pinned omarchy-apple-dev ship.sh as a durable job, sign it, and validate it offline. Without a key it signs with a local TEST identity, which Apple rejects. upload:true sends the IPA to App Store Connect; it never submits for review. The .p8 stays in the owner-only file you name; the key and issuer IDs appear in the job record. A live upload has not been qualified.

key_path.description: Absolute path of the owner-only AuthKey_*.p8 file

description: Run the installed Swift SDK's NDK setup script using the configured ANDROID_NDK_HOME. Required after SDK/NDK installation or relocation.

name: remote.fetch

name: preview.navigate

session.description: Running preview session name; defaults to main

name: preview.configure

description: Set profile, orientation, fold state, insets, guides and zoom without reloading the page.

session.description: Running preview session name; defaults to main

ios_guest.description: The virtual iOS guest display shown by the desktop for a running interactive guest job.

detached.description: Show the guest display as its own phone-shaped window, or dock it back into the dialog. A request to detach made while no interactive guest is running is kept for up to 10 minutes and applied when the guest starts; until then the returned state reports workspace.ios_research.guest.detach_pending as true.

device.description: Select a native device by serial/UDID and attach its existing runtime session.

connect.description: With device: if no runtime session exists yet, the app waits for the device and starts one with its own settings (sound, iPhone runner, Mac). Its window shows the device frame and a startup screen until the stream is live; other sessions are not attached meanwhile. An existing session is shown as it is and never reconfigured.

frame.description: Show the matching native device frame. Never changes the guest hardware or screen geometry.

detached.description: Show the live device as its own frameless, device-shaped window instead of inside the workspace. The same display item moves; no second stream is opened.

pending_avd.description: Name of an Android virtual device that is starting. The device view shows its frame and a startup screen and attaches the real stream once Android has booted. An empty string clears it.

profile_id.description: Device profile for the startup frame of pending_avd or connect.

solo.description: With detached and a device window that is shown or on its way: hide the main window so the device window is the whole app. Closing that window stops its runtime session and ends the app; the device itself keeps running. With unsaved source edits, or once two minutes pass without any device window, the main window returns instead. desktop.open without device_only also brings it back.

description: Run a JSON native Android scenario across devices with device locks, JUnit, JSON reports and failure screenshots.

name: testing.visual_diff
title: Compare with baseline image
description: Compare a PNG screenshot with a baseline PNG pixel by pixel. Reports changed_fraction, changed_bounds and passed (changed_fraction <= threshold); writes a diff image with changes in red when diff is given. update_baseline keeps the actual image as the new baseline instead of comparing.

actual.description: Absolute path of the PNG to check, such as a device.capture result

baseline.description: Absolute path of the approved PNG

diff.description: Absolute path for a difference image: the baseline faded, changed pixels red, ignored regions blue

threshold.description: Largest changed fraction of the compared pixels that still passes

tolerance.description: A pixel counts as changed when a channel differs by more than this

ignore.description: Regions in baseline pixels that are not compared, such as the status bar clock

update_baseline.description: Copy actual to baseline and compare nothing; only after you have checked the image

name: testing.accessibility

Returns structured findings with bounds in pixels and sizes in dp. Heuristics, not a certificate: no contrast, font size or focus order.

device.description: Android serial from device.list; reads the current screen

hierarchy.description: Absolute path of a saved android.hierarchy XML instead of a device

density.description: Screen density in dpi; read from the device when omitted, required with hierarchy

bundle_id.description: Audit only this app's elements, leaving out the status bar and other apps

report.description: Absolute path to also write the result as JSON

name: testing.crashes
title: Find Android crashes
description: Read logcat's crash, system and main buffers and return Java crashes (FATAL EXCEPTION), ANRs and native crashes (Fatal signal) as structured events with package, pid, exception, message, stack and reason. Window: since (epoch seconds on the device clock), the life of job_id, or the last lines lines.

bundle_id.description: Only events of this app and its processes

since.description: Only events from this time on, in seconds since 1970 on the device clock

job_id.description: Only events while this job ran, such as a project.run or testing.run job; uses the computer's clock, which an emulator shares

lines.description: Without since or job_id, how many recent log lines to read

report.description: Absolute path to also write the result as JSON

name: testing.results
title: Read test results
description: Read the JUnit XML results of a project's tests into one summary: totals, suites and each failure with its message and stack. name: ios.emulator.control
title: Operate running virtual iOS
description: Inspect, capture or send input to a live ios.emulator.paravirtual job started with interactive=true. Actions are serialized per guest: one that arrives while another runs waits up to 2.5 s for its turn before ios_control_busy is returned. ios_control_starting means the control monitor is not published yet; ios_control_ended means the emulator has exited while the job is still finishing (hashing its media), so wait for the job instead of cancelling it. Coordinates are normalized from 0 to 1 across the captured display. With input_transport=virtio, click/drag use an absolute mouse. With usb-hid, they use a single touchscreen contact; home sends the HID Consumer Menu usage with emulator-owned release, and status reports actual USB delivery counters. Touch has no hover or multitouch. A persistent client (tomaccoctl mcp) can stream a live contact instead: touch_down presses at x/y and holds the guest's control lane until touch_up, touch_move moves the contact (the same point again only keeps it alive), and touch_up lifts it, at x/y when given. Other control actions wait for that lane meanwhile; file frames do not. A contact without any event for 5 s is lifted, and the client's end lifts whatever it still holds. A one-shot call refuses touch_down with ios_touch_lane_required; touch_up is accepted anywhere and always sends a release. A drag lifts at its end point at once, which a scroll view reads as a fling; with hold_ms it first rests there that long, so the content stops where the contact did. power_button sends the native timed 100 ms GPIO side-button pulse only on the tomacco-vphone machine; it can wake or lock the screen, so acknowledgement never establishes the resulting screen state. key accepts QEMU key names. Input acknowledgement is not proof of a guest UI response; inspect a subsequent screenshot. Screenshots stay in the owned job directory. frame returns an actual PNG data_url (up to 16 MiB) and deletes its temporary capture on success or failure; it is suitable for bounded live preview polling. metrics reads actual QMP CPU state/topology, cumulative block-device I/O counters and TCG cache statistics without pausing or resetting the guest. Host sampling timestamps bound the sequential observations. Unknown TCG fields stay null, unavailable monitor statistics retain their error, and the original text is preserved. Counters and guest-clock lag are not application FPS or CPU utilization. stop requests QMP exit so the durable job can finalize media hashes. With guest control enabled it reserves the framework lane and requires a confirmed idle native worker; pending or unknown work prevents stopping. An acknowledgement does not establish guest OS shutdown or completed storage verification. Follow ios.emulator.report until the job ends; an unconfirmed stop is not replayed automatically. If the emulator cannot be told to exit, the stop record is rewritten without the flush confirmation (guest_storage_flushed false, quit_acknowledged false); a request the client cancels leaves no record and does not stop the emulator. trust_cache_update stops the guest's CPUs, replaces the boot's trust-cache module in guest RAM with the file at path and lets them go on; only for a machine built with vphone-trust-cache-update, and ios.virtual.deploy is the way to use it. text types on the USB keyboard, into what has the focus; a key sent before the field has it is lost, so look at a frame first. iOS reads the keys with the layout of the guest's language: layout follows it unless named.

Use file for a viewer that refreshes several times a second. Fails with ios_frame_file_unavailable when no private runtime directory exists. It also fails with ios_frame_file_unavailable, without asking the emulator for a picture, when the display's uncompressed frame would exceed 64 MiB.

name: ios.emulator.prepare_guest_tools
title: Install native iOS guest tools
description: Revalidate the owned payload, take independent locked snapshots of root/auxiliary/SEP disks and install into unsealed Preboot using a networkless Linux helper. Optional previous_tools permits replacing an exactly matching old payload in the new disk copy, preserving the guest's initialized data. Enables the original monitor virtual ERM setting for launchd SupplementalPaths. Preserves other volumes and the original service cache. Does not activate iOS or boot the guest. Read progress/failures and boot_inputs through ios.emulator.report. development_device optionally configures the non-production virtual device for the original local iOS development activation path; its preparation receipt does not claim activation or scene readiness. previous_graphics explicitly upgrades an existing owned Preboot bundle only after verifying its closed directory, file modes and all previous hashes; the replacement is staged and verified before directory exchange. Unexpected contents and leftover transaction directories are refused.

disk.description: Closed restored virtual root disk. Only a new copy is changed.

previous_tools.description: Optional completed old guest-tools build. Its signatures, exact file inventory, contents and modes must match the closed disk before replacing only those files in the new copy.

graphics.description: Optional exact prepared Metal driver bundle directory. Verifies or installs the bundle at /private/preboot/Cryptexes/ps.bundle in the new private copy. Pair it with a kernel whose MetalPluginName names that location and a trust cache binding the same driver/compiler/bridge identities. Refuses unexpected existing files. Records graphics_payload.

trustcache.description: Exact input cache used by the builder.

device_tree.description: Prepared normal-boot virtual vphone600 device tree.

support.description: Local preparation support containing BusyBox and the APFS helper module.

helper_kernel.description: Linux kernel matching the local APFS module.

output.description: New private installation directory; source disks are preserved.

development_device.description: Opt-in non-production vphone600 VM profile. Sets consistent development-device security properties so the original iOS daemon can select its local activation path. Refuses nonvirtual, retail, recovery or inconsistent identities. No daemon patch, activation response, external request or activation-success claim. Read the actual result with ios.emulator.guest operation=setup.

previous_trustcache.description: Original source cache bound to previous_tools when the new graphics cache differs. Requires previous_tools. Each old/new payload is independently revalidated against its own source cache; file inventory/signature checks remain required.

previous_graphics.description: Exact previous owned graphics bundle to verify before replacing it in the new private copy; requires graphics.

resume.description: Continue a complete private copy refused by host resource pressure before the installation helper started. Requires the original inputs and existing output. Revalidates the payload, boot inputs, locks and all source/copy bytes; preserves the previous failure receipt.

name: ios.emulator.guest
title: Control native iOS guest programs
description:
Call the owned guest service through the active job's private virtio-vsock channel. Requires build_guest_tools agent=true and paravirtual guest_control_backend. One framework request and one status, service-log or cancel request may run at once; nothing connects from outside. Framework requests return request_id: ios.emulator.guest_result follows the latest receipt after a timeout without replaying the request. A timed-out mutation may still execute in iOS and is never replayed automatically. status reports the current worker and, as *_supported flags, what these guest tools offer. Acceptance never verifies a visible scene, and a process or crash observation never proves a process lifetime.
Apps: inspect lists LaunchServices inventory; lookup finds a bundle; install takes a guest .app or .ipa through MobileInstallation (an IPA needs bundle_id) with request-correlated progress; register and open start an app through the original FrontBoard service, keeping native errors and the app's PID; cancel stops the current worker. receive_bundle, policy_add and debug_server are the guest side of ios.virtual.deploy and ios.virtual.debug.
Logs: logs reads bounded owned logs by name, among them development (signing setup and verifier), quiet (tomacco-quiet: services unloaded and its locationd guard), battery, debugserver and buffer_texture (the native Metal buffer-texture observer), and an application's log through its container.
Setup: setup reads SetupAssistant and MobileActivation state. setup_finish, on an activated virtual device, backs up and writes the three setup values through cfprefsd and reads them back; it returns restart_required. restart_ui restarts the interface. flush flushes storage. effects reduced or original sets Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion through the system's setters, which turns the glass materials the renderer cannot draw correctly into plain surfaces. watchdog_scale original or a factor 2..30 sets FrontBoard's FBLaunchWatchdogScale, applied after restart_ui or a reboot; the watchdogs stay active. icon_cache clear moves each IconsCache store aside, deleting nothing, and restarts SpringBoard so that every icon is rendered again. time_zone Area/City sets the system zone through tzlink and reads previous_link and link back. auto_lock never or original sets Settings' Auto-Lock through ManagedConfiguration, or SBDontLockEver when profiled does not take it, and reads it back. Setting a zone or Auto-Lock again is harmless, so a lost reply is automatic_retry_safe; a start sends both itself.
State: screen_state reads SpringBoard's screen-lock, passcode and backlight state; a failed RPC stays unknown, never unlocked. display_state reads the MobileGestalt scale and display tuple against the chosen display-scale. display_refresh asks the system helper to rebuild its display cache after checking the scale locally, and a new display_state must confirm it before a UI restart. foreground_state reads SpringBoard's primary-layout application. graphics_state reads the Metal default device and a process-name snapshot without submitting GPU work. surface_state reads IOSurface metadata for up to four comma-separated decimal IDs; no pixels are accessed. network_state lists the interfaces' IPv4 addresses and tries one name lookup. hardware_probe <IOKit class> counts that class's services. gestalt <key> reads one MobileGestalt answer. developer_mode status or enable reads or arms Developer Mode, effective at the next boot. keyboard_layout reports the guest's language, by whose layout iOS reads a hardware keyboard.
Diagnostics: crash_reports <report name prefix> reads the matching .ips and .crash files of the CrashReporter directories, up to 512 KiB as base64 and with crash_report_identities parsed from the reports; it never removes reports. persistence_probe takes create:<64 hex digits>, read:<same challenge>, classes:<challenge> (one file per protection class A..D) or inode:<digits> (a path and protection class for a boot log's failure). A clean-reboot result needs two separately bound boots with the same challenge.

timeout_seconds.description: Absolute response deadline, including partial reads. A timed-out install/register/open/setup_finish/display_refresh may still execute in iOS. Use ios.emulator.guest_result with the original request_id, then inspect native state before a new mutation. Missing receipts do not establish failure.

bundle_id.description: Installation only. Required for guest IPA archives. Optional for .app bundles, where it must match Info.plist. iOS validates the package identity.

name: ios.emulator.guest_result
title: Fetch result of an iOS guest job
description: Observe a framework request by its request_id, including after the original host timeout: install, register, open, lookup, inspect and application logs. Receipts up to 64 KiB are kept. Reads status and the latest atomic receipt from the live guest within one deadline and returns running, completed (with the actual response) or unknown. ready_for_next_request requires a completed receipt and an idle native worker. An absent or overwritten receipt, or a cancelled or timed-out worker, never establishes that a mutation failed. It does not replay the request, cancel a worker or verify a visible scene. The status read carries request-correlated progress (phase, sequence, optional native_status and percent_complete); progress never overrides a receipt. Recovered crash_reports receipts include crash_report_identities.

request_id.description: The exact ID returned by the original guest framework request or its uncertain-outcome error.

timeout_seconds.description: One absolute deadline covering both read-only guest requests.

name: ios.emulator.prepare_cryptexes
title: Install iOS cryptex files
description: Copy a restored virtual disk and install both original iPhone Cryptex filesystems into Preboot. Rechecks original image digests and every copied file; preserves the sealed System. Optional kernel, boot_manifest and device_tree together prepare original ignition grafts and an explicit, version-pinned research kernel: local exact-byte Cryptex seal pins replace Apple authentication for these two objects only. Optional gpu_trustcache installs the PCC GPU bundle and source-built compiler/bridge with exact hash-pinned executable-mapping exceptions and explicit local platform grants. Optional installer_control permits only the exact original signed installer's otherwise-denied MIG 3404 query through its original kernel handler. Optional development_tools adds one mapping exception for its fully verified owned ARM64e library; requires both preceding options. Offline, durable, cancellable.

disk.description: Closed restored virtual GPT disk; a new independent copy is modified.

gpu_trustcache.description: Optional original vphone600 23E5207q StaticTrustCache IM4P, checked against the imported PCC manifest. Requires all three research inputs and a userland import containing the source-built GPU compiler. Explicitly grants local platform trust and executable mapping to the exact verified graphics CodeDirectories, including the compiler bridge when supplied; does not establish working rendering or Apple authentication.

installer_control.description: Opt-in compatibility for the pinned original iOS installer under native service control. Requires kernel, boot_manifest and device_tree. Only KERN_DENIED for MIG 3404 from the exact signed installd CodeDirectory continues into the original kernel handler; other callers and errors are unchanged. Does not establish successful installation or a visible app.

development_tools.description: Optional completed development-signing guest-tools build. Requires gpu_trustcache and installer_control. Verifies the full payload and pins a local executable-mapping exception to its exact signed ARM64e installer library; other code, native signature/resource validation and app-install results retain their original behavior. Install this same payload separately with prepare_guest_tools.

kernel.description: Explicit opt-in to the local Cryptex research policy. Exact original vphone600 23E5207q decompressed kernel; a private modified copy is emitted. Requires boot_manifest and device_tree.

boot_manifest.description: Existing local DER IM4M used for this restored guest. Its exact bytes are pinned; this does not authenticate it as Apple-signed. Requires kernel and device_tree.

device_tree.description: Prepared normal-boot vphone600 device tree with the same ECID as the restored guest and SEP storage. Requires kernel and boot_manifest.

output.description: New private directory; existing output is never overwritten.

name: ios.emulator.prepare_research
title: Prepare iOS test system
description: Package existing, checksummed full-system research inputs into a new isolated bundle. Runs as a durable job; retains source images. Does not supply display, SEP, native app deployment or a complete iOS simulator.

bootstrap.description: Research bootstrap directory, with manifest.json and image-manifest.json

image.description: Assembled APFS image matching the image manifest

output.description: New bundle directory; existing output is never replaced

exclave.description: Optional matching bundle from prepare_ios_exclave.py; required by exclave-dart inputs

name: ios.emulator.prepare_pmp
title: Prepare PMP firmware
description: Verify the matching T8140 BuildManifest digest, unwrap local PMP firmware and preserve its Mach-O segments in a new ELF bundle. No downloads or instruction changes.

firmware.description: Extracted local firmware tree containing the PMP IM4P

name: ios.emulator.inspect_pmp
title: Check PMP execution
description: Recheck PMP container, payload, executable and source manifest. Inspect isolated ARM64 execution and diagnostic capabilities. CPU family and RAM are explicit laboratory policy; not measured silicon state.

engine.description: QEMU executable with the PMP machine and strict bus/system-register fault tracing

controller.description: Experimental ASC/KIC model with architectural ARM timers and explicit laboratory policies; no independent KIC timer banks, measured silicon behavior or power services.

stop_at.description: Optional ARM64 instruction breakpoint inside the verified executable image. Capture and stop the job without changing guest code.

capture_ram.description: Save the isolated 2 MiB RAM after stopping, with exact physical base and SHA-256 in the report.

cpu_midr.description: Explicit 32-bit laboratory MIDR. Selects firmware CPU setup; does not implement the named silicon or change QEMU max ISA features.

cpu_affinity.description: MPIDR affinity fields only (mask 0xff00ffffff). A single CPU; topology bits may select a different firmware path. Not a measured PMP identity.

name: ios.emulator.pmp
title: Run PMP firmware
description: Execute original PMP ARM64 instructions in isolated memory, optionally with the experimental ASC controller. Capture actual bus faults and CPU registers with bounded logs and cleanup. Shares admission with all iOS jobs. Firmware boot, power services and graphical iOS are not provided.

engine.description: QEMU executable with the PMP machine and strict bus/system-register fault tracing

controller.description: Experimental ASC/KIC model with architectural ARM timers and explicit laboratory policies; no independent KIC timer banks, measured silicon behavior or power services.

stop_at.description: Optional ARM64 instruction breakpoint inside the verified executable image. Capture and stop the job without changing guest code.

capture_ram.description: Save the isolated 2 MiB RAM after stopping, with exact physical base and SHA-256 in the report.

cpu_midr.description: Explicit 32-bit laboratory MIDR. Selects firmware CPU setup; does not implement the named silicon or change QEMU max ISA features.

cpu_affinity.description: MPIDR affinity fields only (mask 0xff00ffffff). A single CPU; topology bits may select a different firmware path. Not a measured PMP identity.

name: ios.emulator.research
title: Start iOS test run
description: Boot a disposable copy of a prepared full-system iOS research image directly on Linux. Capture real platform observations, dedicated serial logs and boot pixels. Identical active requests reuse their job; conflicting iOS jobs are rejected. Completion speaks for those observations only, never SpringBoard or graphical apps.

name: ios.emulator.report
title: Read iOS test run
description: Read an owned iOS job report and its actual diagnostic/frame artifacts. A missing report while queued is pending, not success. For an ios.emulator.paravirtual job the reply also carries stop: the record written when the guest was stopped through ios.emulator.control (whether the native worker was idle and whether the guest confirmed flushing its storage), or null if it ended any other way. After a stop whose exit request failed, the record carries guest_storage_flushed false and quit_acknowledged false.

name: ios.emulator.memory
title: Read PMP memory
description: Read a bounded physical-memory range from a completed PMP RAM capture. Verify its size and SHA-256 before returning exact hex, ASCII and little-endian words; never reads arbitrary host files or a live guest.

name: ios.virtual.status
title: Virtual iOS device: status
description: Read whether a virtual iOS device profile is configured, its current run, phase, guest job and any start or stop that is in progress. A guest job started from another data directory has no guest_state here; that is unknown, not stopped. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. Also reports model (for the next start), running_model (of the current run), running_panel (the current run's panel as WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ:WIDTH_MMxHEIGHT_MM, as its guest job's request gave it to the engine, so a later edit of the profile does not change it; null when that boot named no panel. Without a guest job: the model's own panel, or the profile's display profile for the Home-button phone; null for an unknown recorded model), models (the choice: id, name, panel, and source apple or derived) and guest_ended when the guest has ended on its own since the last start, with guest_saved telling whether it flushed its storage and closed cleanly first (as a session does at its time limit). application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. applications lists the developer apps the profile names (bundle path, bundle_id); the start installs them from the guest-tools build that carries them. phase_started and phase_elapsed_seconds tell when the current phase began and how long it has run, and phases lists each phase of the current start or stop with its started time and seconds (empty for a state written before phases were logged). copy_progress, only in the preparing phase, compares the bytes of the new disk copy with those of its base (bytes_done, bytes_total, percent) and names the preparation's step and disk; a reflinked copy is complete at once. start_disk says whether the next start's disk copy fits in the profile's installs: needed_bytes, free_bytes, reclaimable_bytes (older copies the start deletes first), reflink and enough, the check ios.virtual.start refuses with; the status writes nothing to find out, so on a filesystem that might clone files and lacks room for a full copy enough and reflink are null until a start probes it. Null when the base's disks or the filesystem cannot be read.

name: ios.virtual.configure
title: Set up virtual iOS device
description: Select the prepared profile directory used by ios.virtual.start and ios.virtual.stop. The directory must contain a format 1 profile.json (prepare and boot inputs, graphics bundle, engine, application, installs) and a state.json naming the last closed run. Both are validated; nothing is created or repaired. With model alone, the configured profile is kept and only the device model for the next start changes. add_application, remove_application and application change the profile's own app list and the app the start opens, in profile.json; clang names the clang 22 the start rebuilds guest tools with. With add_application and deploy, the app also goes onto the running phone at once (ios.virtual.deploy, in deploy_job).

model.description: Device model the next start describes the phone as (an id from ios.virtual.status models). Empty: the profile's own description, a phone with a Home button. Takes effect at the next start; the disks stay the same.

add_application.description: Host path of an .app directory built for arm64 iOS to add to the profile's applications. It is inspected first (Info.plist, arm64 executable, only allowlisted entitlements) and refused with the reason otherwise. The next start installs it; when the profile's guest tools do not carry it as it is now, the start rebuilds them with the profile's apps and pins the new signing adapter in a derived kernel itself (clang 22 needed: clang, or a clang-22 on PATH).

add_entitlements.description: Entitlements plist to request for add_application; empty: the executable's embedded entitlements, or only application-identifier.

remove_application.description: Host path or bundle identifier of a listed app to remove from the profile. If it was the app the start opens, the owned diagnostic is opened again.

application.description: Bundle identifier of the app the start opens after boot: the owned diagnostic (io.github.marselnenaj.tomacco.research-app) or one of the listed applications.

clang.description: Host path of the clang 22 executable the start rebuilds guest tools with (profile.json toolchain.clang); empty removes it, so a clang-22 on PATH or the build's recorded toolchain is used.

deploy.description: With add_application: install it on the running phone now, without a reboot. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

deploy_open_app.description: With deploy: open the app afterwards.

name: ios.virtual.apps
title: Apps of virtual iOS device
description: List the apps of the configured virtual iOS device in one place: the owned diagnostic, every app profile.json lists (bundle path, bundle_id, name, display_name, entitlements) with version, build and minimum_os read from its bundle's Info.plist on the host now (bundle_readable false with bundle_error when the bundle is gone; null when it could not be read at all; bundle_id_changed when the bundle now names another identifier), and any app the current run has installed that the profile no longer lists (listed false). installed and installed_cdhash are the current run's record of what a start or ios.virtual.deploy installed; they do not say whether the bundle changed since, which the next start checks itself. opens_at_start marks the app the start opens. Reads files only; no guest is asked.

name: ios.virtual.start
title: Start virtual iOS device
description: Start the configured virtual iOS device as one durable job: prepare a new private disk copy from the last cleanly closed run (reinstalling guest tools and restoring the Preboot Metal driver the guest removes), boot it, attempt passcode-free unlock with Home presses and request the configured app once the native screen-state query confirms unlock. Launch acceptance does not establish a visible application scene. A guest that is already running is adopted. Disks of a run that did not close with verified storage are never reused. Follow progress with ios.virtual.status and job.logs. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. A late screen-query receipt is followed by its original request ID. application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. A start that would make a disk copy is refused with ios_virtual_disk_space, before anything is deleted or copied, when the filesystem of the profile's installs lacks the base's disks plus 1 GiB, counting the older copies the start deletes first; a filesystem that clones files (reflink) needs only the 1 GiB.

open_app.description: False boots and waits for the guest service only.

name: ios.virtual.stop
title: Stop virtual iOS device
description: Flush guest storage, stop the running virtual iOS device, wait for its final report and record whether its disks closed with exit 0 and complete storage hashes. Only such a run is used as the base of the next start.

name: ios.virtual.cleanup
title: Clean up virtual iOS device disk copies
description: Delete older disk copies of the configured virtual iOS device from the profile's installs directory, or with dry_run (the default) only report what would go. Only copies the start recorded as its own (state.json created) that lie directly in installs and are named guest-install* are candidates; the verified base, the current run and a start's attempt are always kept (kept, with the reason). Each copy's files are locked before it is deleted, so a copy a running guest holds is refused with the reason. A guest-install* directory the state does not record is listed under unrecorded and never deleted. copies lists each candidate with path, bytes (allocated on disk; blocks a reflinked copy shares with its base are counted in full) and removed; reclaimable_bytes is their sum and freed_bytes what was deleted. A real cleanup is refused with ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs.

dry_run.description: Only report; delete nothing. false deletes the candidates.

name: ios.virtual.deploy
title: Install app on running virtual iOS device
description: One step from a built .app directory to the app on the running phone, without a reboot: inspect the bundle, sign a copy ad hoc, exchange spare entries of this boot's trust cache for its hashes while the guest is stopped for a moment, send it over the guest channel, name it to the signing adapter, install it through installd and open it. A durable job: follow job.logs, whose deploy events carry each step's seconds. The profile lists the app afterwards, so the next start stages it. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off: use ios.virtual.configure add_application and start it. A boot has 512 spare entries and the adapter's table of the boot takes 32 apps, frameworks and extensions.

bundle.description: Host path of an .app directory built for arm64 iOS.

entitlements.description: Entitlements plist to request; empty: the executable's embedded entitlements, or only application-identifier.

name: ios.virtual.debug
title: Debug process on virtual iOS device
description: Join lldb to one process of the running phone: a durable job holds a TCP port on the host's loopback and, once lldb connects, copies its bytes to /usr/libexec/debugserver in the guest, attached to the target. The first line of job.logs is an event with the port and the lldb command, process connect connect://127.0.0.1:<port>. The app needs get-task-allow (ios.virtual.deploy with such entitlements). One session per job; it ends when lldb disconnects. Anything that reaches this port controls that process, so it listens on loopback only.

target.description: The process's decimal PID or its name.

port.description: TCP port on 127.0.0.1; 0 picks a free one.

name: ios.virtual.crash_reports
title: Save crash reports of virtual iOS device
description: Read the running virtual iPhone's crash reports whose file names start with process (an app's executable name, or any report name prefix) through the guest service, as ios.emulator.guest crash_reports does, and keep each complete one as a file on the host at directory/<owner>/<name> (owner mobile or root). reports lists every match: owner, name, path, bytes, sha256, saved, and the pid, process, capture_time and incident_id parsed from its bytes; a report the guest could not read whole, or with a name or owner that is not a plain report name, has saved false, no path and the reason. Pass a saved path to ios.crash_symbolicate. The guest returns at most three reports per directory and 512 KiB of content in all, by descending file name, which is not crash time; collection_complete false means some were left out, and an empty list never proves that nothing crashed. Reports are never removed from the guest. Without directory, a new directory in Tomacco's data directory is used. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

process.description: Report name prefix, usually the app's executable name

directory.description: Absolute host directory for the reports; created if missing. Empty: a new directory in Tomacco's data directory.

name: ios.virtual.screenshot
title: Screenshot of virtual iOS device
description: Save the running virtual iPhone's current screen as a PNG at path, from the same frame ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer. frame none (default) keeps the picture as it is; rounded cuts the screen's corners round with the radius of the model the phone runs as (square for the Home-button phone) and makes outside them transparent; device also puts a plain black bezel around it, a drawing with rounded outer corners and no buttons, not a picture of the phone. The corner radius is the circular arc of the device catalogue's value, not Apple's continuous curve. MCP returns a PNG of up to 4 MiB inline. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

path.description: Absolute path of the PNG to write, ending in .png; an existing file is replaced.

frame.description: none: the screen as it is; rounded: round, transparent corners; device: rounded screen inside a plain bezel.

name: ios.virtual.record
title: Record virtual iOS device screen
description: Record the running virtual iPhone's screen for seconds into an H.264 MP4 at path, as a durable job: the frames ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer, polled fps times a second and encoded by ffmpeg as they come (ffmpeg must be installed). A frame that has not changed, or a poll slower than one frame, repeats the last picture, so the video lasts as long as the recording; the guest itself draws about 10 changed frames a second on this host. The job's result names the file and counts frames_written, frames_captured and frames_distinct; a phone that stops ends the recording early with what it has (ended_early). Follow it with job.wait and job.logs. One recording at a time. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

path.description: Absolute path of the MP4 to write, ending in .mp4; an existing file is replaced when the recording succeeds.

fps.description: Frames per second of the video, and how often a frame is asked for.

name: update.check
title: Check for updates
description: Report the current version, the latest release, its notes link and whether an update applies. Without manual it uses the network at most once a day, and never when updates.mode is off. With manual, which means the user asked, it asks GitHub now, also when off. Installs nothing.

manual.description: The user asked for this check

name: update.apply
title: Install update
description: Start a durable job that downloads the latest release, verifies its Ed25519 signature and installs it through the journalled installer, rolling back if the new version fails its health check. Refused while a job, a device session or the virtual iOS device runs.

manual.description: The user asked for this installation; needed when updates.mode is off

auto.description: Started by automatic updates: needs updates.mode auto, and skips a version that failed or was rolled back

name: update.status
title: Update status
description: Report the update mode, the last check and installation, a running update job, what blocks an installation now and whether a rollback is available. Uses no network.

name: update.rollback
title: Roll back update
description: Restore the version before the last installed update from the installer's journal. Files changed since that installation are preserved and refuse the rollback.
